issues: Whether a claimant can recover damages for standalone psychiatric injury (with no accompanying physical injury) caused by a manufacturer's or retailer's negligence
What legal test governs recognition of a compensable psychiatric injury in negligence (recognizable psychiatric illness vs mere upset)
Whether a manufacturer/bottler owes a duty of care to a consumer for psychiatric harm caused by discovering a contaminant in a sealed product
Whether the psychiatric injury was reasonably foreseeable as a consequence of encountering a contaminated product
Whether the claim falls under product liability/manufacturer's negligence principles (analogous to Donoghue v Stevenson) or general nervous shock doctrine
What evidence is required to prove causation and the existence of a diagnosable psychiatric condition (as opposed to ordinary distress)
key_facts: Client saw something disgusting/contaminating inside a sealed water bottle
Client subsequently developed depression and anxiety
The claim concerns psychiatric injury alone (no physical harm), against a presumed manufacturer/seller of the product
causes_of_action: Negligence (manufacturer's duty of care / product liability)
Possibly breach of warranty of fitness/quality under sale of goods legislation
search_terms: manufacturer duty of care Donoghue v Stevenson
needs_clarification: Which province/jurisdiction did the incident occur in and where does the client reside (affects which provincial law applies)?
